conclusion: The narrow source-level policy-storage/delegation difference is supported. Runtime oracle behavior remains unobserved.

official_source_identity.provenance: Exact official source bytes archived in the two root packets; read whole and matched the packets' source tables.

findings.fact: ParseTokenFields accepts token_policies as a typed slice and assigns it directly. The logical.Request parameter is unused in this method; no actor-policy subset check or default insertion occurs in this parsing branch.
PopulateTokenData explicitly presents an empty TokenPolicies collection as an empty array. This is role readback behavior; it does not decide the policies of a future issued token.

The complete role-create/update handler parses token fields, upgrades the legacy policies alias, performs its other validity checks, and persists the role. Its request accesses are Operation and Storage; the handler does not inspect the caller's policy set. Core endpoint ACL permission still applies and is not removed by this observation.

A supplied legacy policies value is parsed via ParsePolicies, then propagated to TokenPolicies. Empty string returns empty; a supplied empty slice flows through SanitizePolicies with addDefault=false. The separate nil branch returns default. Therefore the no-default statement must not be generalized to every nil or missing input.
The registered JWT backend's PathsSpecial has unauthenticated login-family paths and seal-wrapped config storage; there is no Root-only role declaration in this source.

JWT role parsing calls policies with add_default=true. The helper adds default unless root is present, then validate_assignment rejects requested root or a non-root actor's non-subset assignment. Empty explicitly supplied policies become a default-containing set in this candidate.

inference.conditional_preconditions: An authenticated non-root caller otherwise passes the endpoint's create/update permission and other role-field validity checks, and its credential policies omit default.
inference.current_candidate_prediction: An empty role-policy request reaches the default injection and then returns the assignment denial before role publication.
inference.official_handler_difference: The inspected official handler/token-field path does not impose that caller-policy subset gate and retains the empty role policy collection.
inference.scope: This is a concrete source-predicted gap and a reason to preserve separate actual oracle cases. No HTTP status, successful publication or future token issuance is asserted without runtime evidence.

relation_to_fixture_fix: The R40 ACL test-only default delegation correction makes that fixture valid under current candidate rules. It does not close the official empty-policy/assignment difference and does not justify rewriting the original no-default HTTP23 matrix.
